insight: For South Korea, hydration breaks in the 2026 World Cup have generally had a positive impact on their momentum, with the team gaining momentum in 4 out of 6 breaks. On average, the team's momentum has slightly decreased at a rate of -0.033 per minute during these breaks, but this is a relatively small drop. When South Korea was pressing before a break, they struggled to maintain momentum, losing it at a higher rate of -0.300 per minute, whereas when they weren't pressing, they were able to maintain or slightly gain momentum at a rate of +0.020 per minute. Overall, these statistics suggest that South Korea tends to benefit from hydration breaks when they're not pushing aggressively, allowing them to regroup and potentially come back stronger.
